evidence.finding: Routing version 24.7 was deployed across all queues at 09:15, exactly at incident onset.
Transfer rate rose from approximately 6.3% at 09:00 to 13.5% at 09:15 and remained elevated.
AHT was near forecast before onset but averaged 38.0% above forecast afterward, remaining 32.4%–43.4% high in every post-onset interval.
Service level fell from 88.2% at 09:00 to 44.7% at 09:15 while ASA increased from 33.7 to 80.9 seconds.
Post-incident service level ranged from 42.7% in Account Support to 70.9% in Escalations, consistent with uneven routing impact.
Scheduled and logged-in staffing remained at 49; productive staffing and adherence were effectively unchanged while occupancy rose to 99.2%.
Offered volume averaged 12.0% above forecast after onset, contributing additional pressure but materially less than the AHT variance.

primary_root_cause_detail: Routing configuration version 24.7 was deployed at 09:15, coinciding exactly with a sustained increase in transfers and handle time. The added handling burden exhausted otherwise stable staffing capacity, reduced throughput, and drove the service-level decline. Impact varied by queue, indicating localized misrouting or routing imbalance.
recommended_actions: Roll back or correct routing configuration version 24.7 and validate routing rules before redeployment.
Audit transfer paths and skill mappings, prioritizing Account Support and Billing.
Monitor transfer rate, AHT, occupancy, ASA, and service level by queue after remediation.
Use temporary overflow capacity while queues recover from the accumulated workload.
Add deployment guardrails and automated alerts for abrupt post-change transfer-rate or AHT increases.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Scheduled and logged-in headcount were constant, productive staffing changed only 0.3%, and adherence remained stable.
Volume was moderately above forecast, but demand alone does not explain the exact-time doubling of transfers and approximately 38% AHT increase following the routing deployment.
No platform event was visible; the only operational event was the routing deployment, and the observed signature specifically reflected increased transfers and handling time.

stakeholder_summary: The service-level incident was most likely caused by the 09:15 routing deployment. Transfers more than doubled, AHT rose about 38%, and unchanged staffing reached near-full occupancy, reducing throughput. Moderately elevated demand amplified the impact, with Account Support and Billing most affected.
